payload.claim: `GateResult.new_failures` defaults to `0` with no way to express "not applicable," so a `skip` or `error` status (where no failure count was ever computed) round-trips indistinguishably from a `pass`/`fail` result that was actually counted at zero. The file gets this exact absence-vs-zero distinction right two classes earlier — `Attempt.new_failures: int | None = None` at line 115 deliberately uses `None` for "an IMPLEMENT/SALVAGE turn that landed commits" where no gate count applies — but does not carry the same treatment into `GateResult`. Per the spec's own note that "a kind whose fields cannot reproduce its call site's line is a defect this spec ships and the next one pays for," `SA-0040`'s renderer will have no principled way to tell "verified zero new failures" from "never assessed" for a `skip`/`error` `GateResult`.
